samples.summary: Backend silently drops a malformed `cliState`, and the new CLI then hangs for 30s and reports a misleading timeout
samples.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` maps any `cliState` that is not a string matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/` to `undefined` (line 31-34) and proceeds with the OAuth flow anyway. `auth.controller.ts:130` then emits a loopback redirect with no `state`. But `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:210` now rejects *every* callback whose `state` does not match, without settling the callback promise — so the user completes the whole GitHub login, sees a bare `400 State mismatch` page, and the CLI sits until the 30s timeout at login.ts:261 and prints `Login timed out`. The two sides disagree: the backend treats an unusable nonce as optional while the CLI treats it as mandatory. An express `?cliState=a&cliState=b` (array) or any nonce outside 16-128 chars reaches this dead end. The guard should fail the request with a clear 400 instead of silently discarding the nonce.

samples.summary: New CLI against a backend that does not echo `state` fails only via a 30s hang with no diagnostic
samples.evidence: The state check at login.ts:210 is unconditional, and a mismatch returns 400 without settling or closing. Any backend older than this change (or one where the guard dropped the nonce) redirects to `/callback?code=…` with no `state`, so `stateMatches(expected, null)` returns false and the flow can only end in the 30s timeout error `Login timed out. Try again with \`wafflebase login\``, which points the user at exactly the action that will fail again. A distinct message for 'callback arrived without the expected state' (still refusing the code) would make the version skew diagnosable.

samples.summary: Dropping the empty-segment rejection is justified with 'the server 404s on it', which is not true for a trailing-slash URL that Express maps onto the collection route
samples.evidence: `seg('')` now returns `''`, so an empty *identifier* (not just an unconfigured workspace) yields a path ending in `/`. Express runs with `strict routing` off, so `/api/v1/workspaces/ws/documents/d/tabs/t/cells/` matches `@Get()` on `ApiV1CellsController` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:45), not the intended `@Get(':sref')` at line 78 — i.e. `HttpClient.getCell(doc, tab, '')` (http-client.ts:355) would silently read the whole tab instead of erroring. I could not find a CLI command that reaches `getCell` with an empty ref today (cells.ts:36-40 guards on truthiness), and I checked that no DELETE/PATCH collection route exists on documents, tabs or api-keys, so nothing destructive is currently reachable — but the docstring's blanket claim that an empty segment 'only produces a path the server 404s on' is wrong, and the relaxation applies to every id, not just `config.workspace`. Scoping the exemption to the workspace segment (or rejecting empty ids at the command layer) would keep the guarantee the comment asserts.

finding.summary: Backend silently drops a malformed `cliState`, and the new CLI then hangs for 30s and reports a misleading timeout
finding.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` maps any `cliState` that is not a string matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/` to `undefined` (line 31-34) and proceeds with the OAuth flow anyway. `auth.controller.ts:130` then emits a loopback redirect with no `state`. But `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:210` now rejects *every* callback whose `state` does not match, without settling the callback promise — so the user completes the whole GitHub login, sees a bare `400 State mismatch` page, and the CLI sits until the 30s timeout at login.ts:261 and prints `Login timed out`. The two sides disagree: the backend treats an unusable nonce as optional while the CLI treats it as mandatory. An express `?cliState=a&cliState=b` (array) or any nonce outside 16-128 chars reaches this dead end. The guard should fail the request with a clear 400 instead of silently discarding the nonce.

verdict.reason: The cited code is present exactly as described (guard maps a non-matching cliState to undefined at github-auth.guard.ts:31-34; auth.controller.ts:130-135 omits &state=; login.ts:210-214 rejects without settling; login.ts:261-269 times out after 30s), so the mismatch is real — but it is not blocking under the Correctness rubric. The only producer of cliState in the repo is packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:46, and login.ts:40 always mints randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') — a 43-char string drawn solely from [A-Za-z0-9_-] with no padding — which always satisfies /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/ and is sent exactly once, URL-encoded (a no-op for that alphabet). Grep for `cliState` finds no second client, so an array-valued or out-of-range nonce cannot arise from the shipped flow. The nonce also round-trips intact server-side (cli-auth.store.ts:34-43 stores it with a 5-minute TTL vs. the CLI's 30s deadline; consumeState:53-59 returns it verbatim), so no legitimate login loses it. If a hand-crafted request did trigger the path, the login must fail either way — the CLI is correctly refusing an unbound authorization code — no session is written, no data is lost, nothing crashes, and a retry succeeds. The only delta versus the proposed fix is a fast clear 400 instead of a slow vague "Login timed out": a diagnostics/UX gap (minor at most), not a crash on a real path, data loss, or a broken core flow.
